input.producingPrompt: Produce the load-analysis summary for the Riverside footbridge, a 40 m single-span steel pedestrian bridge (a Warren truss with a 3.0 m wide deck) over a two-track rail line. State: the design pedestrian load; the design wind action; the first vertical natural frequency and the outcome of the vibration comfort check; and the governing ultimate limit state combination and whether it is satisfied. Return a JSON object. Inputs from the analysis model: design pedestrian load 5.0 kN/m² (national annex); design wind action on the truss 1.8 kN per metre of span (peak velocity pressure 0.94 kN/m²); first vertical natural frequency 2.1 Hz; peak vertical acceleration under the design crowd 0.52 m/s², at an assumed damping ratio of 0.5 %; bottom-chord utilisation at the ultimate limit state 0.86 under the pedestrian-leading combination and 0.91 under the wind-leading combination. Comfort criteria: a first vertical frequency between 1.25 and 2.3 Hz requires a dynamic response check, and the comfort limit is 0.7 m/s².

The comfort criterion is met.","governingUls":"The wind-leading combination governs: bottom-chord utilisation 0.91, against 0.86 under the pedestrian-leading combination. 0.91 ≤ 1.0, so the ultimate limit state is satisfied.","notAssessed":["Lateral pedestrian-induced vibration was not asked for and has not been assessed."]}

rationale.rationale: Each quantity the instruction asks for is stated from the model inputs supplied. The 2.1 Hz frequency falls inside the band that requires a dynamic check, so the check is reported rather than skipped. Both ultimate limit state combinations are compared before the governing one is named.
assumptions: The model inputs supplied are current for this design revision.
limitations: Lateral vibration is outside what was asked and is reported as not assessed.
residualUncertainty: The 0.52 m/s² acceleration depends on the assumed 0.5 % damping ratio; the as-built damping is not yet measured.

input.producingPrompt:
Implement colsummary, a Node.js command-line tool for the site-monitoring team: `colsummary <file.csv> --column <name>` reads a CSV file whose first row names its columns and prints five lines for the named column — `count <n>` (the cells that hold a value), `missing <n>` (the blank cells), and `min <x>`, `max <x>` and `mean <x>`, the mean to two decimal places, each of the three `none` when no cell holds a value. A cell holds a value when it is not blank, and that value must be a decimal number such as 12, -3 or 17.5. Fields follow RFC 4180: a field may be enclosed in double quotes, and a quoted field may hold commas and doubled quotes. It exits 2 with a message on standard error when the file cannot be read, and 1 with a message on standard error when the column is not in the first row, a value is not a decimal number, or the arguments are bad; on either it prints nothing on standard output. Requirements: R1 the five lines; R2 RFC 4180 fields; R3 a blank cell is missing; R4 `none` when no cell holds a value; R5 an unreadable file exits 2; R6 a bad column, value or argument exits 1. Put the CSV parser in src/csv.js, the statistics in src/summarise.js and the command in bin/colsummary.js; package.json must declare "type": "module" and the colsummary bin, with no dependencies. Write unit tests in test/csv.test.js and test/summarise.test.js and tests of the command itself in test/cli.test.js, run them with `node --test`, and record the command and its result in docs/test-report.md.

The output this work requires:
Return an implementation record as a JSON object: the files you created or changed, the test command and its result, the requirements each test file covers, and any limitation or residual defect.
input.answer: {"files":[{"path":"package.json","change":"created"},{"path":"src/csv.js","change":"created"},{"path":"src/summarise.js","change":"created"},{"path":"bin/colsummary.js","change":"created"},{"path":"test/fixtures/readings.csv","change":"created"},{"path":"test/csv.test.js","change":"created"},{"path":"test/summarise.test.js","change":"created"},{"path":"test/cli.test.js","change":"created"},{"path":"docs/test-report.md","change":"created"}],"testCommand":"node --test","testResult":"14 tests, 14 passed on the last run; the first run failed 2 of 14, both on the unrounded mean, fixed in src/summarise.js","coverage":[{"file":"test/csv.test.js","tests":4,"covers":["R2"]},{"file":"test/summarise.test.js","tests":6,"covers":["R1","R3","R4","R6"]},{"file":"test/cli.test.js","tests":4,"covers":["R1","R5","R6"]}],"limitations":["Tested with Node v24.11.1 on Windows only.","A file is read whole into memory."],"residualDefects":[]}

rationale.rationale: I wrote colsummary as the instruction lays it out: the RFC 4180 parser in src/csv.js, the statistics in src/summarise.js and the command in bin/colsummary.js, with package.json declaring "type": "module" and the colsummary bin and no dependencies. Each of R1–R6 has a test: R2 in test/csv.test.js; R1, R3, R4 and R6 in test/summarise.test.js; and R1, R5 and R6 through the command itself in test/cli.test.js, on the fixture test/fixtures/readings.csv. With the files as they now stand, `node --test` passes all 14 tests on its last run; its first run failed two, both on the mean, which was not rounded, and src/summarise.js now rounds it to two decimal places. docs/test-report.md records the command and that result.
assumptions: A column is found by an exact match of its name in the first row; if a name appears twice, the first such column is summarised.
Spaces around a cell's text are ignored, so a cell holding only spaces is blank.
A file that is not valid CSV, a quoted field never closed, exits 1 with a message, as a value that is not a number does.
limitations: Tested with Node v24.11.1 on Windows only.
A file is read whole into memory; files larger than a few megabytes were not tried.
residualUncertainty: A quoted field holding a line break is parsed as one field, but no test covers it.
